description:
FILED s449q (Opus round-7 agent Q), MEASURED while implementing #592's FD_CLOEXEC
half.  It is the OTHER half of the same question, and it corrects #592's premise.

MEASUREMENT (a PCL parent opens a file at fd 5, then spawns a real-perl child
that lists /proc/self/fd), taken with FD_CLOEXEC deliberately DISABLED so the
flag cannot be the cause:

    parent-fd=5 cloexec=0
    child-fds=0,1,2,3        <-- fd 5 is NOT there

So a child spawned through `system` / backticks / `open '-|'` never sees the
parent's descriptors, flag or no flag: every one of those paths goes through
`sb-ext:run-program`, which closes descriptors above 2 in the child unless they
are named in :preserve-fds (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp has eight run-program call
sites, none passing it).

TWO CONSEQUENCES:

1. #592's stated symptom does not reproduce here.  t/io/open.t's ok_cloexec
   rows (perl 116/124/128) fresh_perl_is a child running
   `print open(F,"+<&=$fd") ? 1 : 0`, and under a PCL parent that child ALREADY
   printed "0" -- for this reason, not because the flag was set.  The #592 fix
   is still right (perl really does set FD_CLOEXEC, and `fcntl($fh,F_GETFD)&1`
   is now 1 like perl's), but it is not what those rows were measuring.

2. THE OPPOSITE IDIOM CANNOT WORK: perl programs that DELIBERATELY pass a
   descriptor to a child by raising `$^F` above it (that is what $^F is FOR)
   get nothing under PCL.  `t/run/cloexec.t`'s test_inherited half is exactly
   this, and so is any real program that hands a pipe or a lock file to a
   subprocess by fd number.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): the run-program sites need :preserve-fds carrying the
descriptors whose FD_CLOEXEC is clear -- which is now a well-defined set,
because %p-set-cloexec applies the flag by perl's `> $^F` rule.  Either walk
*p-filehandles* for streams whose fd has the flag clear, or track them as they
are opened.  Note `sb-ext:run-program` also has :directory/:environment
interactions and that %p-open-fork-pipe forks by hand (sb-posix:fork + p-exec)
rather than through run-program -- that path inherits normally and is NOT
affected.

BAR: t/run/cloexec.t's 22 rows are the measurement (skip_all_without_config
'd_fcntl'); probe the two halves separately (test_not_inherited must stay
passing) and check `system`/backticks are unaffected for ordinary programs.
subject: A PCL-spawned child inherits NO descriptor above 2, because SBCL's run-program closes them â perl's `$^F`-raising idiom cannot work
